description: We are a development team building functional tools with open space and Earth data. Our background is in coding and web development, with an emphasis on shipping clean, working prototypes. We are looking for teammates in Earth science, astrophysics, satellites, AI/ML, data analysis, design, hardware, and storytelling. We value clear communication and shared ownership.
summary:
We developed Aegis-DeepSpace, an autonomous edge AI flight surgeon and mission simulation platform engineered to safeguard astronaut health during deep-space expeditions.

It directly addresses the critical challenge of high-latency communication—such as 20-minute Mars signal delays or solar blackouts—where astronauts cannot rely on real-time medical support from Mission Control during sudden emergencies. Operating 100% locally at the edge, AegisDeepSpace continuously synthesizes three predictive pipelines: minimum-dose radiation evacuation routing based on spacecraft shielding and space-weather telemetry, non-invasive vocal biomarker analysis to detect early cognitive fatigue and hypoxia, and a physiological digital twin forecasting bone and muscle loss. A deterministic multimodal risk engine cross-references these compounding anomalies against an offline NASA-STD-3001 clinical knowledge base to deliver immediate, actionable triage protocols.

This project is vital for enabling safe, autonomous human exploration beyond low-Earth orbit, transforming reactive emergency response into proactive, zero-latency clinical care. Furthermore, its offline, low-footprint architecture offers a scalable blueprint for remote terrestrial environments—such as submarines, polar research bases, and disaster-relief zones—where medical specialists and reliable connectivity are out of reach.
details: Aegis-DeepSpace is an autonomous edge AI flight surgeon and mission simulator that protects astronauts during deep-space expeditions when 20-minute Mars communication delays prevent real-time guidance from Earth. It works 100% offline by fusing three predictive pipelines—minimum-dose radiation pathfinding (using NetworkX Dijkstra routing and NASA DONKI telemetry), non-invasive vocal biomarker monitoring for fatigue and hypoxia (via Whisper STT, PyTorch 1D-CNN on MFCCs, and DistilBERT), and a physiological digital twin forecasting bone and muscle loss (combining Frost’s Mechanostat ODE with Scikit-Learn gradient boosting)—into a deterministic risk engine backed by an offline NASA-STD-3001 RAG knowledge base. Built with Python, React, Next.js, TypeScript, and Three.js, the project uniquely models compounding multi-system health risks without intrusive wearables, providing zero-latency, explainable clinical protocols designed for extreme spaceflight constraints and adaptable to remote Earth environments like submarines or polar stations.
